nodes.name: slider
nodes.title: Number Slider
nodes.description: a bounded numeric parameter.
nodes.panics: `value` lies outside `min..=max` or the bounds are inverted — a drifted literal is a loud red, never a silent clamp.

inputs.name: step
inputs.doc: Snap increment for the canvas widget and scrub caching (doc 12);

nodes.name: toggle
nodes.title: Boolean Toggle
nodes.description: an on/off parameter.

nodes.name: panel
nodes.title: Panel
nodes.description: display sink; shows counts and samples on the canvas.

inputs.name: data
inputs.doc: Anything — the panel shows whatever arrives.

nodes.name: series
nodes.title: Series
nodes.description: an arithmetic sequence of numbers.
nodes.panics: `count` is negative — loud refusal, never a silent empty list (the scheduler turns node panics into red nodes, stage 3).

nodes.name: random
nodes.title: Random
nodes.description: seeded uniform random numbers in a domain.
nodes.panics: `count` is negative.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.doc: The interval values are drawn from (uniform).

nodes.name: add
nodes.title: Add
nodes.description: sum of two numbers.

nodes.name: construct_domain
nodes.title: Construct Domain
nodes.description: a numeric interval from its endpoints.

nodes.name: deconstruct_domain
nodes.title: Deconstruct Domain
nodes.description: the endpoints of an interval.

nodes.name: subtract
nodes.title: Subtract
nodes.description: difference of two numbers.

nodes.name: multiply
nodes.title: Multiply
nodes.description: product of two numbers.

nodes.name: divide
nodes.title: Divide
nodes.description: quotient of two numbers (IEEE: dividing by zero yields ±∞).

nodes.name: modulo
nodes.title: Modulo
nodes.description: IEEE remainder of `a / b` (sign follows `a`).
nodes.panics: `a % 0` is NaN, which value construction refuses — the node goes red.

nodes.name: power
nodes.title: Power
nodes.description: `a` raised to `b` (`^` in expressions).

nodes.name: remap
nodes.title: Remap
nodes.description: map a value linearly from a source domain to a target domain. Values outside the source domain extrapolate linearly (no clamping).
nodes.panics: the source domain is empty (`start == end`) — the map is undefined there.

inputs.name: source
inputs.doc: The domain the value lives in.

inputs.name: target
inputs.doc: The domain to map it into.

nodes.name: item
nodes.title: List Item
nodes.description: one element of a list by index. Selecting an absent (`Optional`) slot yields an absent element — `E` carries the `?`, so the output is `Point?` exactly when the list is `[Point?]`.
nodes.panics: the list is empty, or when `index` is out of range and `wrap` is off.

inputs.name: wrap
inputs.doc: Wrap out-of-range indices around the list (modular).

nodes.name: length
nodes.title: List Length
nodes.description: the number of slots in a list (absent slots included — slot-preserving nulls keep their places, docs/08 rule 6).

inputs.name: list
inputs.doc: The list — absent (`Optional`) slots count too.

nodes.name: flatten
nodes.title: Flatten
nodes.description: one nesting level removed: the inner lists concatenated in order (`[[a, b], [c]]` → `[a, b, c]`). One level only, always (docs/09: `flatten_all` for every level, and says so); absent inner slots are preserved as absent slots of the output.
nodes.panics: an OUTER slot is absent (a missing inner list — refused at marshalling with its index: optional lists have no representation, so there is nothing slot-preserving to do with one); the node itself has no other refusal.

nodes.name: partition
nodes.title: Partition
nodes.description: consecutive groups of the given sizes (`[a, b, c, d]` with sizes `[1, 3]` → `[[a], [b, c, d]]`). Slot-preserving: absent slots land in their group as absent slots.
nodes.panics: a size is negative (the offending index and value in the message) or when the sizes do not sum to the list's slot count (both counts in the message) — never a silent short or padded last group.

inputs.name: sizes
inputs.doc: Consecutive group sizes; they must sum to the list's slot count.

nodes.name: chunk
nodes.title: Chunk
nodes.description: consecutive groups of `size` slots; the last group may be short (GH Partition List). Slot-preserving: absent slots land in their group as absent slots; an empty list chunks to no groups.
nodes.panics: `size < 1`.

inputs.name: size
inputs.doc: Group size (the last group may be shorter).

nodes.name: concat
nodes.title: Concat
nodes.description: `a` then `b`, one list (GH Merge for two lists). Slot-preserving: absent slots of either input keep their places in the output.

nodes.name: cull
nodes.title: Cull
nodes.description: keep the slots where the pattern is true and drop the rest, returning the kept list and the index map back into the source (the sanctioned way elements leave a list — identity survives).
nodes.panics: the pattern's length differs from the list's slot count — strict zip, both counts in the message (GH's repeating Cull Pattern is the silent-mismatch behavior docs/09 retires).

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.doc: Keep the slot where true, drop it where false — one entry per slot

outputs.name: kept
outputs.doc: The kept slots, in order (absent slots kept as absent when their

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: Provenance: `map[i]` is the source index of `kept[i]` (docs/08 rule 6).

nodes.title: Construct Point
nodes.description: a point from x/y/z coordinates.

nodes.name: deconstruct_point

nodes.name: unit_x

nodes.title: Vector 2Pt
nodes.description: the vector from `a` to `b`, optionally unitized.
nodes.panics: `unitize` is on and the points coincide within tolerance — a zero vector has no direction.

inputs.name: unitize
inputs.doc: Normalize the result to unit length.

nodes.name: xy_plane
nodes.title: XY Plane
nodes.description: the world XY frame at an origin.

nodes.name: xz_plane
nodes.title: XZ Plane
nodes.description: the world XZ frame at an origin.

nodes.name: yz_plane
nodes.title: YZ Plane
nodes.description: the world YZ frame at an origin.

nodes.name: construct_plane
nodes.title: Construct Plane
nodes.description: a frame from an origin and two axes: x unitized, y orthonormalized against x (Gram–Schmidt), so the stored plane is a right-handed orthonormal frame with normal x × y.
nodes.panics: `x` has no length at tolerance, or `y` is parallel to `x` at tolerance (its component off the x line has no length) — red with the measured length, never a NaN frame.

inputs.name: y
inputs.doc: The y direction (any length; its component along x is removed, then

nodes.name: line
nodes.title: Line
nodes.description: a straight segment between two points.

nodes.name: polyline
nodes.title: Polyline
nodes.description: a vertex chain, open or closed.

inputs.name: closed
inputs.doc: Close the chain (implicit edge from the last vertex to the first).

nodes.name: circle
nodes.title: Circle
nodes.description: an analytic circle in a plane. The stored frame is orthonormalized at construction, so downstream evaluation is exact.
nodes.panics: the radius is not above tolerance or the plane's axes are degenerate (zero-length or parallel).

nodes.name: rectangle
nodes.title: Rectangle
nodes.description: an analytic rectangle in a plane, always closed. The frame is orthonormalized at construction. (The rounded-`corner` parameter arrives with compound curves, v0.1.)
nodes.panics: either extent is empty at tolerance or the plane is degenerate.

inputs.name: x
inputs.doc: Extent along the plane's x axis.

inputs.name: y
inputs.doc: Extent along the plane's y axis.

nodes.name: divide_curve
nodes.title: Divide Curve
nodes.description: points, tangents, and parameters at equal arc-length steps. An open curve yields `count + 1` samples (both ends included); a closed curve yields `count` (the seam appears once).
nodes.panics: `count < 1` or the curve is degenerate at tolerance (no usable length, zero radius, collapsed frame).

nodes.name: as_closed
nodes.title: As Closed
nodes.description: the checked closed-curve refinement (docs/08 rule 5). Already-closed curves pass through unchanged; an open polyline whose endpoints coincide within tolerance closes (duplicate end vertex dropped).
nodes.panics: the curve cannot close: a line, endpoints apart beyond tolerance, or fewer than 3 distinct vertices after closing — red with the distance that failed, never a silent pass (wall lesson 13).

nodes.name: extrude
nodes.title: Extrude
nodes.description: extrude a closed planar profile into a watertight prism (mesh-backed under its v0.1 name, doc 15).
nodes.panics: the profile is degenerate or non-planar at tolerance, the direction lies in the profile plane, `segments < 3`, or the profile polygon is self-intersecting.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.doc: The closed, planar profile to extrude.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.doc: Extrusion direction and length (need not be normal to the profile —

nodes.name: loft
nodes.title: Loft
nodes.description: a ruled solid between two closed sections, capped at both ends (the wall's frusta: Voronoi cell → tip cap; cones and chamfers from circle → circle). Sections pair vertex `i` with vertex `i` (polylines vertex-to-vertex as given — no resampling, seam = vertex 0; analytic sections tessellated to `segments` vertices starting at the plane's x axis), walls are two triangles per quad, caps are ear-clipped (non-convex sections welcome), orientation is fixed by signed volume and the result is re-verified watertight. Lift with `each()` to loft per part (`loft(start=each(cells), end=each(caps))`).
nodes.panics: the vertex counts differ (both counts in the message), a section is open, degenerate at tolerance, non-planar, or self-intersecting, the sections wind in opposite directions, the sections coincide or are coplanar (zero volume), `segments < 3` for an analytic section, or the result is not watertight.

inputs.name: start
inputs.doc: The first closed section (the wall's base cell).

inputs.name: end
inputs.doc: The second closed section (the wall's tip cap) — same vertex count as

inputs.name: segments
inputs.doc: Tessellation density for analytic sections (circles, rectangles):

nodes.name: box
nodes.title: Box
nodes.description: an axis-aligned box in a plane's frame (mesh-backed under its v0.1 name, doc 15). Decreasing domains are normalized.
nodes.panics: any extent is empty at tolerance or the plane is degenerate.

inputs.name: x
inputs.doc: Extent along the frame's x axis.

inputs.name: y
inputs.doc: Extent along the frame's y axis.

inputs.name: z
inputs.doc: Extent along the frame's z axis.

nodes.name: sphere
nodes.title: Sphere
nodes.description: a UV sphere at a plane's origin (mesh-backed under its v0.1 name, doc 15).
nodes.panics: the radius is not above tolerance, `segments < 3`, or the plane is degenerate.

inputs.name: plane
inputs.doc: Center frame; the plane's z is the polar axis.

inputs.name: segments
inputs.doc: Longitudinal segment count (latitude bands follow as half).

nodes.name: mesh_union
nodes.title: Mesh Union
nodes.description: the union of watertight meshes via Manifold (docs/08: watertight, parallel, seconds).
nodes.panics: Manifold refuses an operand (named by index) — its ε-validity is stricter than structural watertightness in corner cases.

inputs.name: meshes
inputs.doc: The solids to union (empty list → the empty solid).

nodes.name: mesh_difference
nodes.title: Mesh Difference
nodes.description: subtract every cutter from a mesh via Manifold; the result may be the empty solid. Lift with `each()` to carve per part (`mesh_difference(mesh=each(frusta), cutters=each(cutter_groups))`).
nodes.panics: Manifold refuses the mesh or a cutter (named by index).

inputs.name: cutters
inputs.doc: The solids to subtract (the wall's carve: one part, its cutters).

nodes.name: mesh_intersection
nodes.title: Mesh Intersection
nodes.description: the intersection of two watertight meshes via Manifold; the result may be the empty solid.
nodes.panics: Manifold refuses an operand.

nodes.name: as_watertight
nodes.title: As Watertight
nodes.description: the checked watertight refinement (docs/08: the mesh-tier solid): every edge shared by exactly two consistently oriented triangles.
nodes.panics: the mesh has open or inconsistently oriented edges — red with the count, never a silent pass (wall lesson 13).

nodes.name: voronoi
nodes.title: Voronoi
nodes.description: planar Voronoi cells of seed points, clipped to a convex boundary. Cells are index-aligned with the seeds (provenance never shifts). Spike scope: the boundary must be convex and everything must lie on its plane.
nodes.panics: the boundary is open, non-convex, or degenerate; when a seed is off the boundary plane, coincides with another seed within tolerance, or owns no area inside the boundary; or when `seeds` is empty.

inputs.name: seeds
inputs.doc: Seed points — one cell per seed, index-aligned.

inputs.name: boundary
inputs.doc: Convex closed boundary the cells are clipped to.

outputs.name: cells
outputs.doc: One closed cell per seed, index-aligned with `seeds`.

nodes.name: move
nodes.title: Move
nodes.description: translate geometry along a vector.

nodes.name: rotate
nodes.title: Rotate
nodes.description: rotate geometry about a plane's normal through its origin.
nodes.panics: the plane is degenerate (zero-length or parallel axes).

inputs.name: angle
inputs.doc: Rotation angle in radians (right-handed about the plane's normal).

inputs.name: plane
inputs.doc: Rotation frame: about its z axis, through its origin.

nodes.name: scale
nodes.title: Scale
nodes.description: uniform scale about a center. Negative factors point-reflect (mesh orientation is preserved by winding correction).
nodes.panics: `|factor|` is within tolerance of zero — geometry would collapse to a point.

nodes.name: orient
nodes.title: Orient
nodes.description: the rigid motion carrying the source plane onto the target plane (the wall's part-to-plate workhorse).
nodes.panics: either plane is degenerate.

inputs.name: source
inputs.doc: The frame the geometry currently sits in.

inputs.name: target
inputs.doc: The frame to carry it onto.

nodes.name: linear_array
nodes.title: Linear Array
nodes.description: `count` copies stepped along a direction, the first at the original position.
nodes.panics: `count < 1`.

inputs.name: count
inputs.doc: Number of copies (the first sits at the original position).

nodes.name: custom_preview
nodes.title: Custom Preview
nodes.description: display a geometry with a color; the display cost shows in the profiler next to compute cost.

inputs.name: geometry
inputs.doc: The geometry to draw (lift with `each()` for lists).

nodes.name: text_tag
nodes.title: Text Tag
nodes.description: a display-only text label at a plane.

inputs.name: location
inputs.doc: Where the tag sits (the plane orients it).

nodes.name: export_obj
nodes.title: Export OBJ
nodes.description: write meshes to a Wavefront OBJ file for external viewers (the stage-4 debug window into headless geometry; the real exporters — 3MF, DXF — arrive with the wall corpus).
nodes.panics: the file cannot be written (missing directory, permissions) — an export that silently wrote nothing is the worst outcome (wall lesson 7).

inputs.name: meshes
inputs.doc: The meshes to write — ANY meshes (this is the debug viewer's door;

inputs.name: path
inputs.doc: Output path (`.obj`); relative paths resolve against the working

nodes.name: text_outlines
nodes.title: Text Outlines
nodes.description: glyph contours as closed polylines (béziers flattened to `segments` per curve span), laid out left-to-right from the plane origin along +x with the baseline on the x axis; `size` is the capital-letter height; a newline in `text` stacks lines downward by `line_gap` × `size`, left-aligned. Fonts are bundled in the binary (reproducibility); the spike bundles `DejaVu Sans Bold` only. One curve per contour, in text order then the font's contour order; whitespace advances the pen and yields no curve.
nodes.panics: the font is not bundled (the message lists the bundled names), `size` is not above tolerance, a glyph is missing from the font (names the character), `segments < 1`, or the plane is degenerate.

inputs.name: text
inputs.doc: The text to set; `\n` starts the next line.

inputs.name: size
inputs.doc: Capital-letter height (cap height) in document units.

inputs.name: plane
inputs.doc: The frame: text runs along +x from the origin, baseline on the x

inputs.name: segments
inputs.doc: Chords per bézier span when flattening the outlines.

inputs.name: line_gap
inputs.doc: Baseline-to-baseline distance between lines, in multiples of `size`.

nodes.name: text_solids
nodes.title: Text Solids
nodes.description: one watertight solid per glyph (counters handled: the glyph region is triangulated with its holes), extruded `depth` along the plane normal (negative = the other way), same layout as `text_outlines` (cap-height `size`, baseline on the plane's x axis, newline stacks lines by `line_gap` × `size`). Glyphs of several pieces (`i`, `%`, `"`) are one mesh with several shells; whitespace yields no solid. The wall's label deboss cutters.
nodes.panics: `text_outlines` would (the font is not bundled — the message lists the bundled names —, `size` is not above tolerance, a glyph is missing from the font — names the character —, `segments < 1`, the plane is degenerate), when `depth` is within tolerance of zero, or when a glyph's contours cannot be triangulated into a watertight prism (touching or self-intersecting outlines — a font defect, named by character).

inputs.name: text
inputs.doc: The text to set; `\n` starts the next line.

inputs.name: size
inputs.doc: Capital-letter height (cap height) in document units.

inputs.name: depth
inputs.doc: Extrusion depth along the plane normal (x × y); negative extrudes

inputs.name: plane
inputs.doc: The frame: text runs along +x from the origin, baseline on the x

inputs.name: segments
inputs.doc: Chords per bézier span when flattening the outlines.

inputs.name: line_gap
inputs.doc: Baseline-to-baseline distance between lines, in multiples of `size`.
